pairs.question: O felix, tantis quem primum industria rebus prodidit auctorem! deus ille an proxuma divos mens fuit, in caecas aciem quae magna tenebras egit et ignarum perfudit lumine vulgus?
pairs.answer: Arcadium stat fama senem, quem Maenalus auctor et Lacedaemoniae primum vidistis Amyclae per non adsuetas metantem retia valles Dercylon.
pairs.derivation: Authorial question: the poet asks who first invented the hunting art, and whether the inventor was a god or a godlike mind. Setup retained (o felix...auctorem!) so the interrogative 'deus ille an...' has its referent (the auctor). The framing line 'dic age Pierio (fas est) Diana, ministro' (an invocation narrating the asking) is dropped per the speech-tag/framing rule. Answer starts at the operative reply 'Arcadium stat fama senem...' and ends at the first full stop after the name 'Dercylon', which is exactly what answers the 'who' question; the following sentence 'haut illo quisquam se iustior egit...' praises him and is cut as elaboration. Inline verse numbers 95 and 100 stripped; no editorial angle brackets present.
